title: UI: Improve landmark navigation
body:
Closes #32271

## What I did


[Peek 2026-01-09 19-27.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22d5de78-2f03-4f2f-9fa6-5540cdc3e00f)

* [x] Aligned site structure with feedback from accessibility experts who audited our recent a11y changes
* [x] Applied landmarks to
 * Sidebar (`header` element, `banner` role, was previously a nav)
 * Search (`search` role)
 * Explorer (`nav` role)
 * Preview (`main` role)
 * Toolbar (`region` role)
 * Addon panel (`aside` role)
* [x] In mobile, applied `header`/`banner` to the MobileNavigation bottom bar
* [x] Added global keyboard shortcuts for landmark nav (F6 / Shift+F6) based on React Aria, so that everyone can keyboard nav like a pro
* [x] Added focus outline specific to landmark regions so they can be spotted (reviewed with @MichaelArestad)
* [x] Fixed focus outline visibility on preview region
* [x] Fix issue with nav being unreachable when Search is focused
* [ ] ~Fix preview iframe eating up F6 key events~ (can't find a way)

Still gotta handle a few focus / keyboard handling edge cases.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

Not tested

#### Manual testing

##### With screen reader
1. Run Storybook with NVDA or VoiceOver on
2. Use your screen reader's landmark navigation shortcuts (NVDA: D and Shift+D, when in browse mode)
3. NVDA will show a decorative outline (NVDA baked-in feature), VoiceOver won't

##### Without screen reader
1. Run Storybook in your favourite browser
2. Press F6 and Shift+F6 to quick nav between landmarks, using [React Aria's hook](https://react-aria.adobe.com/useLandmark)
3. Notice the highlight that helps you spot in which region you are
4. Notice the quick nav remembers which element of the landmark region you were last on, and returns to that element
5. This quick nav also does not suffer from limitations between browse mode and focus mode in screen readers

### Limitations

* Can't quick nav from within the preview iframe with React Aria shortcut
* Can't change the keyboard shortcut, it is hardcoded by React Aria, so we can't show it in the shortcuts UI for it to be customised
* Quicknav feature is undocumented at the moment

### Documentation

@kylegach @jonniebigodes @MichaelArestad I'd like to get your opinions on how to make this feature discoverable to users. Should we add it in the shortcuts page, even though it can't be edited, just for visibility? Is there a best page to document it in the docs website?

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Why not `ComponentProps<typeof CardOutline>`? That seems more functionally correct/complete and is our usual pattern for forwarded props.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
ComponentProps of a styled component have incompatible signatures with DOM attributes for attrs like style.

Here, I need a "*Props" prop because rest properties aren't injected in the root of the component, so it's not possible to pass intrinsic HTML elements to it.

In our case in particular, all the props of CardOutline are hard-coded by Card, and aren't supposed to be publicly exposed.

I've renamed the property `outlineAttrs` to make it clearer what it can or cannot contain.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using ComponentProps<typeof CardOutline> instead of the current type, implying a code change.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body:
What I don't like about this is that it suggests that both Explorer and SearchResults might be rendered at the same time. The Swap component was there to make it very explicit that that would never be the case. An if/else ternary on a single condition seems more appropriate.

Also, I worry that by unmounting rather than hiding, these components will lose important internal state when switching between explorer and search. Have you checked that?

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
The Swap component forced both components to always render, but be unreachable. This leads to landmark elements being findable in the DOM, but not focusable.

Depending on the landmark navigation algorithm in use (react-aria, NVDA, VO, JAWS, Narrator, etc), this can lead to bugs where navigating to the next landmark does nothing (it finds the landmark, but fails to focus it). So we need to distinguish states where nav is kb-reachable (we are in the input but there's no query) and states where nav is entirely hidden (we have a query and results).

Note that the "recently opened" view and the "search results" view have never been kb-reachable. This does not change here as it's a Tree 2.0 issue to be solved.

You were right about loss of state in the tree though, so I've reworked the code to keep rendering the Explorer (still with a distinction between visually hidden and not reachable).

The SearchResults view is necessarily stateless, as it relies on the `query`, and it can only change/disappear when the `query` changes or disappears. I prefer to render it only when necessary if that's ok with you.

--

@MichaelArestad we should probably jam on the UX surrounding "recently viewed" for Tree 2.0, as it's both hard to discover and I wouldn't be able to make it keyboard-accessible with the current UX logic.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using an if/else ternary instead of current approach, and raises a concern about unmounting causing state loss that should be investigated/fixed.

comments.author: coderabbitai

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Typo in `hardcodedShortcuts` causes `goToPreviousLandmark` to remain editable.**

`'gotoPreviousLandmark'` has a lowercase `t`, but the actual key in `shortcutLabels` and the API is `'goToPreviousLandmark'` (uppercase `T`). This mismatch means the shortcut won't be marked as hardcoded and users will be able to "edit" it (though changes won't take effect since react-aria ignores custom bindings).

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-const hardcodedShortcuts = ['gotoPreviousLandmark', 'goToNextLandmark'];
+const hardcodedShortcuts = ['goToPreviousLandmark', 'goToNextLandmark'];
```
</details>

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Why did you move `<IconSymbols />` from Tree to Sidebar? Is that because Tree is no longer rendered when SearchResults is open, but SearchResults also uses these icons?

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
I moved it because this code was misplaced.

It's what loads the SVG that is then referenced through svg [use](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Element/use), but it was loaded in the tree even though it was consumed both in the tree and in the search results.

That made it mandatory to render (and hide) the nav tree in all instances so that icons would appear in search results.

By moving the SVG resource up in the DOM to the parent of either instance, I ensure it's available when needed without creating implicit rendering dependencies.

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure question seeking understanding of why IconSymbols was moved, with no implied suggestion or request for change.
